recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-11315; future molecular variation example changes should be handled as new CG/MolecularDefinition work rather than restoring retired Sequence.pointer behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-11315 was a Published FHIR-core Sequence change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2, asking whether Sequence.pointer represented complex variants and phase; the accepted clarification was to add a complex-variant example using CIGAR and explain sequence.pointer as linking relative sequences for genome graph use.
initial_application: Git commit c45e176baeebb2d365ecf5cd92b465ed031680f3 explicitly referenced #11315 and added source/sequence/sequence-complex-variant.xml with a CIGAR-bearing variant plus example spreadsheet registration, so the original legacy Sequence issue was applied.
additional_context: The current build no longer uses the legacy Sequence/MolecularSequence pointer model: source/fhir.ini comments out molecularsequence as a resource and uses moleculardefinition for CG, diagnostics-module.html says MolecularSequence has been replaced by MolecularDefinition, FHIR-37413 removed MolecularSequence.pointer and pointer examples, FHIR-37414 removed the CIGAR attribute, and later cleanup removed residual MolecularSequence references.
reconciliation: An empty no-change audit commit was published. Re-adding the old pointer/CIGAR example would conflict with later Published decisions and with the current MolecularDefinition model, which represents complex sequences through relative edit operations and examples.
